m1 - A/B RULING on the statement-vs-clause merge: option A (keep the merge, rename as an explicit statement-level acceptance adapter, document the divergence). Sent to the engineer at msg-01M172DSD8Q22CE0H52HWJNN12. Recorded here with the measurement, which is the part worth keeping.

MEASURED before ruling, production segmenter over all ten paraphrases: ONE OF TEN diverges. Precise yields 2 production units; every other paraphrase yields exactly 1. The merge is a no-op for nine of ten.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CAPACITY-TO-FAIL TEST, and I made this required rather than optional: pin THE NUMBER and name the case, not 'at least one'. An existence assertion stays green if the segmenter later splits five of them, which is exactly the drift the test exists to catch.

BONUS THE MEASUREMENT SURFACED: the single divergent case has 2 production units AND 2 declared targets. So the objection that per-clause gold cannot be assigned without inventing evidence holds in general but may not bind for Precise specifically. Worth a docstring sentence so the next person does not conclude the door is shut when it is merely closed.

B rejected, and the reason belongs in the code rather than in a thread: copying statement targets onto every clause would invent evidence, and a fixture that invents gold is worse than one that admits a coarser grain. Same principle as not renormalising residue - the honest coarse answer beats the fabricated fine one.
